summary:
SARView is a map-based project for exploring where changing soil moisture may need a closer look. It covers agricultural areas in multiple Indian cities, including Nagapattinam, Ludhiana, and Ahmedabad. Users can explore locations and compare satellite observations to help guide where to investigate.

Satellite readings over Nagapattinam showed a decrease in surface moisture across the study area. SARView makes satellite information easier to explore and provides a starting point for local checks and agricultural planning. With more satellite data, the project could expand to additional cities and regions around the world.
details:
Link: https://k3shavc0des.github.io/KMAHackathonProject/

SARView helps users explore soil-moisture changes across agricultural areas in Nagapattinam, Ludhiana, and Ahmedabad. Its interactive map lets people move between cities, zoom into areas, and compare satellite readings. This makes satellite information easier to explore and can help users decide where local observation may be useful.

For NISAR observations, SARView compares locations measured on different dates, applies the data’s quality checks, and shows how surface moisture changed. The team chose this approach to make comparisons more consistent. Results are grouped into map areas so users can see regional patterns. The project uses NASA satellite data and an interactive web map; no special hardware is required.

SARView brings observations from multiple cities into one map-based experience. The team considered data quality, observation dates, map scale, and the difference between surface moisture and conditions deeper in the soil. Suitable local SMAP data was unavailable for this analysis, so it could not be included as regional context. With more satellite data, SARView could expand to additional cities and regions around the world, helping more communities explore local moisture patterns. Future work could also add SMAP readings when suitable data is available.
